definition: Encumber means to weigh down with a load that hampers movement or freedom.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word encumber. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know encumber should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Decades of borrowing encumbered the railway with debts that no fare increase could outrun.
An inconvenience is a pebble in the shoe — mildly bothersome; it stops far short of encumber.
Immobilize goes further than encumber — an encumbered mover still inches forward; an immobilized one cannot move at all.

A burden is the plain, often emotional word for a heavy load someone must carry — worries, costs, responsibilities. Encumber is more active in feel: whatever encumbers you tangles your movement or freedom, hampering each step rather than simply weighing on you.

To saddle someone is to dump a duty, debt, or chore on them in one stroke — you are saddled with the paperwork the moment it lands. Encumber describes the ongoing drag of the load itself, hampering movement or progress long after it arrives.

When Marisol inherited her aunt's bakery, she expected long hours; she did not expect the paperwork that came folded inside the deed.
The building carried a decades-old loan, two liens from a remodel in the nineties, and a lease clause requiring written approval for any new oven.
Each obligation, taken alone, looked survivable, but together they encumbered the business at every turn.
She could not repaint the storefront without a lender's signature, could not add a second register without an inspection, could not even move the counter.
The bakery still opened at six each morning and still sold out by noon — but every step forward dragged, as if the shop wore ankle weights.
